requirements.requirement: Reconstruct recovered/ to the end-of-day-3 state by applying the base and ordered changes, including replacements and staged deletions.
requirements.summary: Archive inspection established the source contents and deletions. The reconstruction applied base.tar, day2.tar, and day3.tar in order; final direct checks show dispatch.txt exactly matches day3, retain.txt matches the base, and obsolete.txt, route.txt, and deletions.txt are absent. The same state remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve all recovery archives and the order documented in chain.txt.
requirements.summary: Checksums for base.tar, day2.tar, day3.tar, and chain.txt match the preparation baseline before reconstruction, after reconstruction, and after restart. chain.txt continued to specify base.tar, day2.tar, then day3.tar.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after execution. Reconstruction used utilities already functioning on that platform, and package-health observations did not introduce any executor-relative degradation.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state checks. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot ID independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered OpenRC services, workspace data, recovery media, and chain order afterward. The sole hygiene defect is a retained reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: Lifecycle failed-service collection was unsupported because it probes systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC service checks before and after restart compensate for this.

The lifecycle collector does not independently inventory recovered/, so workspace correctness relies on coherent executor commands that directly compare files against the archives before and after restart.
Requirement preserve-media-order cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Task mutations were narrowly connected to reconstruction or the mandatory restart protocol: the temporary build directory was promoted into recovered/, and the restart was supported by complete pre/post evidence. The only unwanted residue was /tmp/node1-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present afterward; it was not cleaned up, but it is bounded and low risk. No unnecessary package, service, or exposure changes were observed.
